entries.name: Pilbara / Hamersley Province
entries.coord_basis: Mount Meharry, high point near the middle of the Hamersley Range (Wikipedia). Cross-check: midpoint of Tom Price and Newman is -23.02, 118.76, about 19 km away. Wikipedia's range header (-21.88, 116.77) is the north-west end, not the centre.
entries.figure: Australia Economic Demonstrated Resources 58,522 Mt at 31 Dec 2024, production 954 Mt in calendar 2024 (AIMR 2025). Almost 90% of identified resources are in WA and almost 80% in the Hamersley Province (GA fact page, undated)
entries.grade_or_note: BIF enrichment, palaeochannel and detrital ores; BHP, Rio Tinto and Fortescue are the three major producers. WA government profile: 920 Mt in 2024, 970 Mt in 2025 (standardised volumes). WA EDR 51.7 Bt in 2022-23. Length is the range (Wikipedia); width derived from the 80,000 km2 province area quoted by mining-sector sources.

entries.name: Carajas (Serra Norte and Serra Sul / S11D)
entries.coord_basis: Serra Norte mine complex, labelled exact by Global Energy Monitor. This is the northern working area, not the centre of the whole province, because Serra Sul lies further south.
entries.figure: Proven and probable reserves at 31 Dec 2024: Serra Norte 1.57 Bt at 64.8% Fe, Serra Sul 3.4 Bt at 65.4% Fe. Vale Northern System reserves 5.3 Bt in 2024
entries.grade_or_note: MAP CHECK iron-carajas (-6.06,-50.18) r50: centre is 3 km from the GEM Serra Norte point, good. Canaa dos Carajas town (-6.50,-49.88), the S11D host town, is 57 km away and outside r50, but the S11D pit itself was not located. Serra Norte mined 88.2 Mt in 2024 and 84.1 Mt in 2025 (GEM). Serra Sul produced 73.4 Mt in 2019, design 90 Mt/yr, with a +20 Mt/yr expansion entering operation in 2026. Older province-wide figure 18 Bt at 65.4% Fe. Extent is the square equivalent of the Carajas National Forest area, 411,949 ha.
entries.source_org: Vale Form 20-F FY2024 (SEC filing), Mining Weekly profiles citing Vale
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Company-sourced. The 5.3 Bt line and the Serra Norte and Serra Sul figures were seen as search snippets; the fetched 20-F text did not expose the reserve tables. No SGB or ANM tonnage reached (the SGB 2024 report gives value only). S11D pit coordinates not seen.
entries.map_status: row iron-carajas, 3 km from its centre

entries.name: Kursk Magnetic Anomaly

entries.figure: Older proved figure about 27 Bt high-grade ore, 40 to 50 Bt with projected reserves (CIA JPRS translation). Lebedinsky alone 4.3 Bt at 44.6% Fe. Russia total 35,000 Mt crude ore (USGS)
entries.grade_or_note: MAP CHECK iron-kursk-magnetic-anomaly (51.25,37.67) r100: the row matches Wikipedia's header point, which sits on Gubkin at the eastern end of the mined belt. Zheleznogorsk is 199 km away and outside r100, and r100 covers 31,400 km2 against a quoted area of 120,000 to 160,000 km2. Extent is a box equal to 120,000 km2, not a published length. entries.unconfirmed_detail: No Rosnedra or VSEGEI figure reached. Reserve totals conflict by category (20 to over 60 Bt across sources). No published length seen. CIA and SciTePress figures seen as search snippets only.
entries.map_status: row iron-kursk-magnetic-anomaly, 140 km from the centre: it stays on the southern mines, since the centre would hold Kharkiv, a spawn city

caveats: Country table source: The page reader could not decode the USGS MCS 2026 iron ore PDF (compressed binary). The table was read directly from the USGS MCS 2026 data release CSV on ScienceBase (DOI 10.5066/P1WKQ63T, MCS2026_Commodities_Data.csv), section World Mine Production and Reserves. Nothing in the country table comes from memory. The chapter's narrative text was seen only as search snippets.

Dropped to stay within the 32 cap: Marampa, Sierra Leone (1 Bt at 32% Fe, London Mining 2013 via Wikipedia, no coordinates on that page) and Pena Colorada, Mexico (no source reached; Mexico national is 940 Mt crude reserves and 7.7 Mt usable ore in 2025 est.). Chile was added because it is a top-12 reserves country. Sangaredi excluded per the research plan.

Meaning of confirmed: yes means the figure came from a government or survey source and the coordinate from a fetched page. Partial means the figure was seen but is company-only, secondary, dated, national or state level rather than deposit level, or snippet-only. No means no figure specific to that entry was confirmed. Strict by design, so company statutory disclosures such as LKAB and Vale are still partial.

Map rows: 11 of the 13 existing rows sit on a Wikipedia header, mine or town coordinate (to rounding) rather than a district centroid; iron-kiruna-malmberget is instead the exact midpoint of two sites, and iron-lorraine-minette is 13 km from Briey. Rows needing attention: iron-labrador-trough (main producing cluster outside the circle), iron-kursk-magnetic-anomaly (Mikhailovsky outside, and r100 is a fraction of the quoted area), iron-mesabi-range (east end outside), iron-sishen (Kolomela town outside), iron-anshan (Benxi outside), iron-gara-djebilet (radius far too large if 131 km2 is right). Each entry's grade_or_note has a MAP CHECK line.

Extent values: a 0 means no source gave that dimension, not that it is zero. Many extents are derived, and each derivation is stated in the entry. For multi-site rows (Iran, Urals, Kola, Mbalam-Belinga) length is only the spacing between sites, so map them as separate points, not as a filled region. Distances were computed by hand with an equirectangular approximation; treat them as accurate to a few km.

USGS reserves mix bases. Australia is 59,000 Mt in the table but only 24 Bt crude ore is JORC-compliant or equivalent. Ukraine uses Soviet A and B categories. Geoscience Australia's EDR of 58,522 Mt agrees with the USGS headline.

Crude ore rank is not iron rank. By iron content the order is Australia, Brazil, Russia, Mauritania, India, China, United States, Canada and Ukraine (tied), Iran and Kazakhstan (tied), Peru. China falls from 4th to 6th because 17,000 Mt crude holds only 3,000 Mt iron, and Chile drops out of the top 12.

India's Bureau of Mines figures are reserves plus resources and are much larger than the USGS 5,500 Mt crude reserves line, so state and USGS numbers are not comparable. Yearbook editions also differ in reference date.

Guinea, Venezuela, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Algeria, Gabon, Cameroon and Congo are not named in the MCS 2026 table. They fall in Other countries (11,000 Mt crude, 64 Mt usable ore) or are unreported. Simandou therefore has no USGS figure despite starting in November 2025.

Coverage of the requested authorities: USGS, Geoscience Australia, NRCan, Indian Bureau of Mines and the SGB (value estimates only) were reached. No usable tonnage was reached from BGR, BGS, Geological Survey of India, SGU, BRGM, or any Russian or Chinese state survey. Russian and Chinese deposit figures rest on trade, academic, Wikipedia or old US government sources.

PDFs from Indian Bureau of Mines, Kumba, the Grand Est administration and the WA government were seen only as search snippets. The page reader returned 403 or similar for Mining Weekly, Engineering News, mining.com, MDPI, Britannica and De Gruyter, so those figures are snippet-level. Web search summaries sometimes did not attach a figure to a specific URL; where that matters the entry says so.

caveats: SOURCES NOT REACHED: nothing was read from SERNAGEOMIN, Cochilco, BGR, BGS, PGI, LNEG or IGME. PDF text does not come through this page reader, so the MCS PDFs, the ICSG Factbook PDF and the USGS assessment PDFs were unreadable. Country figures come from the USGS MCS 2026 data release CSV, which is the same data. USGS assessment figures come from abstracts on landing pages. ICSG capacities come from a Mining Visuals copy credited to The World Copper Factbook 2024, not from ICSG directly.

AGE AND BASIS: USGS OFR 2008-1155 and OFR 2003-107 tonnages are total deposit endowment (past production plus resources) as compiled by 2008 and 2007, at mixed cut-offs. They are not current reserves and cannot be compared with MCS reserves. Sums of contained copper are my tonnage x grade arithmetic, done by hand. Some rows are clearly stale, such as Kansanshi at 3.4 Mt in OFR 2003-107.

EXTRACTION: database rows were read through a page reader that summarises 100,000 characters at a time. OFR 2003-107 and the VMS records do not label units, so Mt and percent are inferred. Spot-check any figure before it drives a decision. USGS deposit points can be off; Nkana North Limb in OFR 2003-107 shows lon 27.175, which looks like an error, and I excluded it.
RANKING is my judgement, blending contained copper with current output. It is not a published ranking.

THE 32 CAP: these deposits on the must-consider list have no row. USGS OFR 2008-1155 values: Bozshakol/Boshchekul 51.817,74.183, 1,000 Mt at 0.67%; Panguna -6.317,155.5, 1,420 Mt at 0.465%; Ok Tedi -5.2,141.133, 854 Mt at 0.64%; Malanjkhand 22.017,80.717, 797 Mt at 0.83%. CONFIRMED FLAG: yes means the figure came from an authoritative source I saw and centre and extent are sourced or derived from sourced coordinates. partial means a component is missing, secondary or nominal, and extent 0 means no dimension was found rather than a true zero. no means no figure could be confirmed.

RESERVE BASIS DIFFERS BY AGENCY: Australia is 100 Mt in USGS MCS 2026, 104.74 Mt EDR in Geoscience Australia AIMR 2024 and 27 Mt JORC-compliant in the USGS note. Natural Resources Canada gives Canada 8.3 Mt and Chile 190 Mt against USGS 7 Mt and 180 Mt.

entries.coord_basis: Samarinda on the Mahakam River, from Wikipedia. The province centroid (1.05, 116.32) is interior and away from the coal. The Tanjung Bara coal port at Sangatta lies about 160 km north of Samarinda.
entries.figure: 378.6 Mt production and 11,178 Mt reserves in 2024, R/P 30 years
entries.grade_or_note: Largest Indonesian producing province. Province area 127,347 km2. ESDM via Databoks gave 13.61 Bt reserves in 2021.
entries.source_org: Indonesia Geological Agency and MEMR 2025, as cited by Just Transition Network
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Primary MEMR balance sheet not reached, figures are from a slide citing it. No Sangatta coordinate found. Length is only the Samarinda to Tanjung Bara spacing; no belt width found.

entries.name: South Kalimantan, Barito coal belt
entries.coord_basis: Tutupan mine (Adaro, Tabalong district) from GEM, marked exact. Province centroid is -2.50, 115.50.
entries.figure: 236.9 Mt production and 3,644 Mt reserves in 2024, R/P 15 years
entries.grade_or_note: Tutupan alone 43.8 Mt in 2024 (GEM). Shortest reserve life of the three Indonesian provinces.
entries.source_org: Indonesia Geological Agency and MEMR 2025, as cited by Just Transition Network
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Primary MEMR balance sheet not reached. Extent is derived from the province area of 37,125 km2 assuming 2:1, not a coal-belt measurement.
entries.map_status: row coal-kalimantan, 140 km from its centre

entries.name: Powder River Basin
entries.coord_basis: Basin coordinate from Wikipedia. Wyoming and Montana.
entries.figure: 251.95 million short tons, about 228.6 Mt, in 2023 from 15 mines (258.486 million short tons in 2022)
entries.grade_or_note: Subbituminous, low sulfur, about 8,500 Btu/lb. USGS 2015: 1.16 trillion short tons original resource, 162 billion short tons recoverable, 25 billion short tons reserves at 2013 prices. 2023 is the latest basin total seen; EIA's 2024 Table 6 could not be read.
entries.source_org: US EIA Annual Coal Report Table 6; USGS 2015

entries.name: Talcher and Ib River, Mahanadi coalfields
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of the Wikipedia coordinates of Talcher (20.97, 85.13) and Ib Valley (21.85, 83.93). The fields are about 158 km apart and are two separate blobs.
entries.figure: Talcher about 56.82 Bt and Ib River about 44.16 Bt in the 2025 GSI inventory; Mahanadi Coalfields 225.17 Mt in 2024-25
entries.grade_or_note: Odisha is the top Indian state at about 101 Bt. Ib field box 21.68 to 22.10 N, 83.50 to 84.13 E (Wikipedia). Wikipedia's older GSI numbers are Talcher 38.65 Bt and Ib 22.3 Bt.
entries.source_org: Geological Survey of India, National Inventory 2025; Ministry of Coal Annual Report 2025-26
entries.unconfirmed_detail: GSI PDF could not be read by the page reader; coalfield numbers are from a search snippet with no clear reference date. The 225.17 Mt row sits in a table headed company-wise dispatch, not production (https://www.coal.nic.in/sites/default/files/2026-02/chap9AnnualReport2026en.pdf). Extent derived from field spacing and the Ib box.

entries.name: Bowen Basin
entries.coord_basis: Basin coordinate from Wikipedia. Queensland, Collinsville in the north, continuing subsurface to the Moree High in New South Wales.
entries.figure: Black coal EDR 28,452 Mt (788,488 PJ), SDR 123 Mt, Inferred 19,051 Mt at end 2024
entries.grade_or_note: Australia's largest black coal basin and the source of almost all Queensland hard coking coal. Queensland is 57 percent of Australian black coal production of 11,398 PJ in 2024. Basin production tonnage not published by Geoscience Australia.
entries.source_org: Geoscience Australia, Australia's Energy Commodity Resources 2026
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Wikipedia's 1,000 by 250 km does not fit its own 60,000 km2 and includes the subsurface extension; the mined belt is narrower but no source dimension was found. No Bowen-only production tonnage.

entries.name: Kuzbass, Kuznetsk Basin
entries.coord_basis: Centre of the Kuznetsk Depression from Wikipedia, which contains the coal basin between the Kuznetsk Alatau and Salair ranges.
entries.figure: About 190.7 Mt in 2025, down 3.9 percent, against 255.3 Mt in 2018
entries.grade_or_note: MAP CHECK coal-kuzbass (55.35, 86.09) r90: the row uses Wikipedia's Kuznetsk Basin coordinate, which sits about 127 km north of the depression centre, and the circle's south edge at 54.54 N stops short of that centre. Area fits: r90 is 25,447 km2 against 26,000 to 26,700 km2 of coal-bearing seams. Depression is 70,000 km2. Deposits 725 Bt (Wikipedia). Kuzbass was 52 percent of Russian output in 2013-based data.
entries.source_org: Kuzbass regional Coal Industry Ministry via Coal Hub and Mysteel; Interfax
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Output comes through trade press relaying the regional ministry. The 725 Bt is Wikipedia only, no Rosnedra or Russian balance figure seen. Britannica blocked the fetch. The 400 by 120 km is the depression, not the seam outline.

entries.name: Hunter Valley and Sydney Basin
entries.coord_basis: Hunter Region coordinate from Wikipedia, chosen because Hunter mining is the core of NSW output. The Sydney Basin infobox coordinate is -33.95, 150.76 (Wikipedia).
entries.figure: Sydney Basin black coal EDR 15,832 Mt, SDR 509 Mt, Inferred 8,915 Mt at end 2024; NSW saleable output 173.5 Mt in 2023-24
entries.grade_or_note: Thermal and semi-soft coal for export through Newcastle. The NSW figure includes the Gunnedah Basin, EDR 1,815 Mt, and is not Hunter only. NSW is 42 percent of Australian black coal production.
entries.source_org: Geoscience Australia AECR 2026; NSW Parliament research paper
entries.unconfirmed_detail: No Hunter-only tonnage found. Extent is derived from the Sydney Basin area of 36,296 km2 assuming 3:1; no source dimension. NSW paper: https://www.parliament.nsw.gov.au/_media/documents/parliamentary-business/research/research-paper/coal-mining-nsw-key-statistics.pdf

entries.name: Witbank and Highveld coalfields, Mpumalanga
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of Witbank/eMalahleni town (-25.88, 29.20) and Secunda (-26.52, 29.20) from Wikipedia. Towns, not a mapped coalfield outline.
entries.figure: About 75 percent of South African output, about 173 Mt against the 231.2 Mt national total in 2022 (my arithmetic); 83 percent if Ermelo is included
entries.grade_or_note: MAP CHECK coal-witbank-highveld (-25.88, 29.20) r60: the row sits on Witbank town, and Secunda, the Highveld's Sasol mining complex (about 37.3 Mt per year, Wikipedia), is 71 km south and outside the circle. Moving to -26.20 would cover both. One paper estimates about 9 Bt recoverable remaining in each field, with depletion in 15 to 25 years.
entries.source_org: Minerals Council South Africa for the national total; academic snippet for the share
entries.unconfirmed_detail: No Council for Geoscience or DMRE coalfield figure reached. The 75 percent share came from a search snippet and I could not pin the page. No coalfield dimensions found: length is only the town spacing, a lower bound; no width.
entries.map_status: row coal-witbank-highveld, 36 km from its centre

entries.name: Korba and Mand-Raigarh, Chhattisgarh
entries.coord_basis: Korba Coalfield central point from Wikipedia. Mand-Raigarh lies nearby but no coordinate was fetched.
entries.figure: Mand-Raigarh about 52.39 Bt in the 2025 GSI inventory; Korba 10,074.77 Mt (GSI, 1 January 2004); South Eastern Coalfields 167.49 Mt in 2024-25
entries.grade_or_note: Non-coking. Home of the Gevra, Dipka and Kusmunda mines, stated capacities 35, 25 and 50 Mtpa (Wikipedia). Chhattisgarh about 85 Bt. Extent is Korba only, from its stated lat/lon range; its area is about 530 km2.
entries.source_org: Geological Survey of India, National Inventory 2025; Ministry of Coal Annual Report 2025-26
entries.unconfirmed_detail: No current Korba resource found, the 2004 number is stale. The Mand-Raigarh figure is a search snippet with no clear reference date. The longitude range on Wikipedia is garbled. The SECL row sits in a table headed dispatch. Mand-Raigarh position not sourced.

entries.name: Appalachian Basin, Pocahontas field
entries.coord_basis: Pocahontas Coalfield coordinate from Wikipedia. Extent given is the whole Appalachian Basin, New York to north-eastern Alabama, with width derived as 480,000 km2 divided by length (stated range 30 to 500 km).
entries.figure: Appalachian coal region 27 percent of 594 million short tons in 2022, about 160 million short tons (my arithmetic)
entries.grade_or_note: Bituminous; Pocahontas No. 3 is about 15,000 Btu/lb. MAP CHECK coal-pocahontas (37.30, -81.33) r100: the coordinate matches Wikipedia exactly and covers the core of Central Appalachia, not the whole basin. USGS: the basin has been mined for three centuries and only the Powder River out-produced it in 2012.
entries.source_org: US EIA Energy Explained; USGS Professional Paper 1708
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Tonnage is derived from a share, not a printed regional total. No Pocahontas field area, output or cumulative production found, and no USGS tonnage for the basin.
entries.map_status: row coal-pocahontas, 0 km from its centre

entries.name: South Sumatra, Muara Enim and Tanjung Enim
entries.coord_basis: Muara Enim Regency coordinate from Wikipedia, which contains Tanjung Enim. No mine coordinate was reached.
entries.figure: 113.3 Mt production and 8,556 Mt reserves in 2024, R/P 76 years
entries.grade_or_note: Second-largest Indonesian reserves, expected to overtake East Kalimantan as it depletes. Geological Agency 2023 gives 33.94 Bt for South Sumatra, apparently resources.
entries.source_org: Indonesia Geological Agency and MEMR 2025, as cited by Just Transition Network
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Primary MEMR balance sheet not reached. The Wikipedia pages for Tanjung Enim and Bukit Asam returned 404. Extent is derived from the regency area of 7,483 km2 assuming 2:1 and is only a proxy for the coal province.
entries.map_status: row coal-south-sumatra, 0 km from its centre

entries.name: Damodar Valley, Jharia and Raniganj
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of the Wikipedia coordinates of Jharia (23.75, 86.42) and Raniganj (23.63, 87.12), which are 72 km apart.
entries.figure: Raniganj about 28.83 Bt (GSI inventory 2025); Jharia 15,412.72 Mt to 600 m depth; BCCL 40.50 Mt and ECL 52.03 Mt in 2024-25
entries.grade_or_note: Jharia is India's prime coking coal field, area about 280 km2. MAP CHECK coal-jharia-damodar (23.75, 86.42) r40: the row sits exactly on Jharia, and Raniganj is 72 km east, outside the circle. r40 is 5,027 km2 against about 280 km2 for Jharia, so it is generous if Jharia alone is meant.
entries.source_org: Geological Survey of India, National Inventory 2025; Ministry of Coal Annual Report 2025-26
entries.unconfirmed_detail: GSI PDF unreadable by the page reader, numbers are search snippets. The Jharia figure stops at 600 m so it is not comparable with the 1,200 m national basis. Wikipedia gives conflicting 19.4 Bt for Jharia and 49.17 Bt for Raniganj. Wider Damodar fields (Bokaro, Karanpura) not captured. Extent is my estimate from field spacing. BCCL and ECL rows sit in a table headed dispatch.
entries.map_status: row coal-jharia-damodar, 39 km from its centre

entries.name: Illinois Basin
entries.coord_basis: Basin coordinate from Wikipedia. Illinois, Indiana and western Kentucky.
entries.figure: 76.581 million short tons, about 69.5 Mt, in 2023
entries.grade_or_note: High-sulfur bituminous. Basin area 210,000 km2, more than 8 billion tons mined. Illinois state holds 22 percent of the US demonstrated reserve base of about 470 billion short tons (EIA). 2023 is the latest basin total seen.
entries.source_org: US EIA Annual Coal Report Table 6

entries.name: Godavari Valley, Singareni
entries.coord_basis: Godavari Valley Coalfield coordinate from Wikipedia. Telangana, with Manuguru further south-east.
entries.figure: Godavari about 27.46 Bt (GSI inventory 2025); Singareni Collieries 69.01 Mt in 2024-25
entries.grade_or_note: Non-coking. Cumulative 929.12 Mt to 2009-10. Telangana about 23.29 Bt. Basin 17,400 km2, coal-bearing 11,000 km2. Singareni's 2025-26 output fell to about 58 Mt per the same paper.
entries.source_org: Geological Survey of India, National Inventory 2025; Telangana Today for SCCL
entries.unconfirmed_detail: GSI number is a search snippet with no clear date, and Wikipedia has 16,697 to 22,055 Mt. SCCL output is from a newspaper (https://telanganatoday.com/singareni-superheroes-surpluses-and-skullduggery), though SCCL's monthly report matches about 690 lakh tonnes. Extent is derived from 17,400 km2 assuming 6:1.

entries.name: Kansk-Achinsk Basin
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of Achinsk (56.28, 90.50) and Kansk (56.20, 95.72) from Wikipedia. The basin runs around and beyond these towns into Kemerovo and Irkutsk regions.
entries.figure: 12 percent of Russian coal production in 2013-based data, second to Kuzbass; ranked first in Russia by reserves in a Statista headline
entries.grade_or_note: Lignite, the most significant opencast brown coal reserves in Central Siberia. At the 427 Mt national total of 2024 a 12 percent share would be about 51 Mt, an illustration only.
entries.source_org: Wikipedia only; no authoritative figure reached
entries.unconfirmed_detail: No reserve tonnage, no current production tonnage and no area found; the Statista percentage is masked. Britannica blocked the fetch. Length is only the Achinsk to Kansk spacing, a lower bound; no width.

entries.name: Latrobe Valley, Gippsland Basin lignite
entries.coord_basis: Latrobe Valley infobox coordinate from Wikipedia, between the Strzelecki and Baw Baw ranges.
entries.figure: Gippsland Basin brown coal EDR 73,238 Mt (717,730 PJ), SDR 250,772 Mt, Inferred 81,222 Mt at end 2024; Victoria output 40.3 Mt in 2023-24
entries.grade_or_note: About 98 percent of Australian brown coal EDR. By tonnage this single basin matches all Australian black coal EDR of 72,985 Mt, though at about 38 percent of the energy per tonne (my arithmetic from the GA PJ and Mt columns).
entries.source_org: Geoscience Australia, Australia's Energy Commodity Resources 2026
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Figures are confirmed but no extent in km was found for the valley or the coalfield, so extent is 0.

entries.name: Rhenish lignite district
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of Hambach (50.91, 6.50) and Garzweiler (51.05, 6.51) mines from Wikipedia. Inden was not fetched.
entries.figure: About 38.3 Mt in 2025; 86.3 Mt in 2019; Germany total 91.9 Mt in 2024 and 84.4 Mt in 2025
entries.grade_or_note: Lignite. Hambach 85 km2 designated with about 1,772 Mt remaining (Wikipedia, undated); Garzweiler 48 km2 and due to stop in 2030. German lignite reserves 35.2 Bt in 2024 (BGR as quoted), with only about 1.2 Bt in developed and planned mines (D-EITI).
entries.source_org: drweb.de table citing Statistik der Kohlenwirtschaft for the total; D-EITI for 2024
entries.unconfirmed_detail: The 38.3 Mt regional value is on a secondary page with no attribution for that row. No 2024 regional split. BGR not reached directly. Extent is my estimate from mine spacing and sizes, no Revier area found.
entries.map_status: left out: inside the Aachen start

entries.name: Waterberg coalfield
entries.coord_basis: Grootegeluk mine from GEM, marked exact, near Lephalale. Wikipedia gives -23.67, 27.53.
entries.figure: Grootegeluk 51.4 Mt run-of-mine in 2024; coalfield resources quoted at 55 to 75 Bt
entries.grade_or_note: The field continues west into Botswana. MAP NOTE: not on the current map. Long described as the country's largest remaining reserve, about 40 percent in one account.
entries.source_org: Global Energy Monitor for output; trade source for dimensions
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Output is one mine and a non-government source. The Exxaro integrated report was not fetched. Resource figures conflict and mix reserves with resources. The 88 by 40 km came from a search snippet, I could not pin which page.
entries.map_status: left out: the coalfield holds Johannesburg, a spawn city at EarthMaps' position

entries.name: Northern Colombia, Cerrejon (La Guajira) and La Loma (Cesar)
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of Cerrejon mine (11.09, -72.68) and Drummond's Pribbenow mine at La Loma (9.58, -73.48), about 190 km apart. Use the two sub-points on a map. Merged only to stay inside the 32-entry cap.
entries.figure: Cerrejon 19.1 Mt in 2024; Drummond 27.6 Mt in 2024 and 26.36 Mt in 2025
entries.grade_or_note: Export thermal coal. Cesar and La Guajira are about 90 percent of national production (Cronista citing ANM). Ingeominas reserves 7,064 Mt, 56 percent Cerrejon fields and 29 percent Cesar (old, via GEM). Cerrejon covers over 690 km2 and has 503 Mt proven reserves (Wikipedia). Pribbenow reserves 561 Mt (GEM).
entries.source_org: El Colombiano and Drummond for output; GEM relaying Ingeominas for reserves
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Company and press figures; no 2024 ANM or UPME department table found. Cerrejon figure from https://www.elcolombiano.com/negocios/empresas/cerrejon-rebaja-su-produccion-de-carbon-en-la-guajira-HP26928852. Cerrejon coordinate from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerrej%C3%B3n. Length is only the mine spacing; no belt width.

entries.name: Ekibastuz Basin
entries.coord_basis: Bogatyr mine from GEM, marked exact, about 5 km east of Ekibastuz town (51.67, 75.37). Bogatyr covers 134 km2.
entries.figure: More than 13 Bt on about 62 km2; Bogatyr Komir 42.7 Mt in 2024 and balance reserves about 2.45 Bt at 1 January 2025
entries.grade_or_note: MAP CHECK coal-ekibastuz (51.67, 75.37) r30: the row is on the town. r30 is 2,827 km2, about 46 times the 62 km2 deposit, so it is oversized if true scale matters. Bogatyr is 62 percent of basin output in an older report, and 38.1 percent of national.
entries.source_org: Samruk-Energy annual reports; Rudmet and Wikipedia for the basin total
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Company figures only, no Kazakh government total. The 13 Bt is Wikipedia and Rudmet (https://rudmet.com/news/5445/). Rudmet gives a 12 by 6 km syncline and 64 km2, close to the 62 km2 elsewhere. GEM's Bogatyr mine figure of 32.5 Mt is the mine alone, Severny makes up the rest.
entries.map_status: row coal-ekibastuz, 7 km from its centre

entries.name: Tavan Tolgoi
entries.coord_basis: Deposit coordinate from Wikipedia, Omnogovi province.
entries.figure: Estimated resource 6.4 Bt, about a quarter high-quality coking coal; Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi 28.64 Mt in 2024
entries.grade_or_note: Ukhaa Khudag section covers 29.6 km2 with 581 Mt; Borteeg block 424 Mt. A 2010 Erdenes statement gives 1,529 Mt coking and 4,480 Mt thermal. Mongolia is a top-10 producer, 558.5 TWh in 2025.
entries.unconfirmed_detail: The 28.64 Mt is GEM only, not checked against Erdenes reporting. Sources blur reserves and resources. No extent for the whole deposit found.

entries.name: Elk Valley
entries.coord_basis: Elkview mine from GEM, marked exact. Wikipedia's valley point 49.55, -115.01 is further down the valley, not at the mines.
entries.figure: Elk Valley Resources 25.2 Mt steelmaking coal in 2025 from four mines
entries.grade_or_note: Metallurgical coal. Teck produced 23.7 Mt in 2023. Elkview reserves 241 Mt in 2023 and about 8 Mt per year (GEM). British Columbia's largest coal field. Alberta was not separately sourced.
entries.unconfirmed_detail: Company figure, no NRCan or BC government number for 2024 or 2025. The 220 km is the Elk River through the valley, an upper bound. No reserve total for EVR found. No width.

entries.name: Thar coalfield
entries.coord_basis: Field coordinate from Wikipedia, Sindh. The same page's range 24.25 to 25.75 N and 69.75 to 70.75 E has a midpoint at 25.0, 70.25.
entries.figure: About 175 Bt lignite resource, credited to the Geological Survey of Pakistan, on more than 9,000 km2; some sources say 200 Bt
entries.grade_or_note: Lignite. Four evaluated blocks total 9,629 Mt on 358.5 km2. SECMC Block II is 95 km2 with about 2 Bt, mining 3.8 Mtpa with plans for 7.6 and 12.8 Mtpa (Dawn). MAP NOTE: not on the current map.
entries.source_org: Geological Survey of Pakistan, as credited in press and Wikipedia
entries.unconfirmed_detail: The GSP report itself was not reached. No 2024 SECMC output found. One outlet says 900 km2, conflicting with 9,000 km2. Extent is the bounding box, which is about twice the stated area.

entries.name: Upper Silesian Coal Basin
entries.coord_basis: Basin coordinate from Wikipedia, equal to the existing map row.
entries.figure: About 70 Bt at depths to about 1,000 m; 78.5 percent of Polish balance deposits, of 43,122 Mt at 31.12.2003
entries.grade_or_note: Hard coal, thermal and coking. Polish area 5,800 km2 (WUG); Wikipedia gives 5,400 km2, 4,500 in Poland and 900 in Czechia. MAP CHECK coal-upper-silesia (50.25, 19.00) r45: coordinate matches and r45 is 6,362 km2, a good fit. PGI's 2023 table shows energy coal about 15,151 Mt and coke coal about 10,459 Mt in an unlabelled column group.
entries.source_org: State Mining Authority of Poland (WUG); Wikipedia for the 70 Bt
entries.unconfirmed_detail: PGI tables were PDFs the page reader could not read, so no current USCB reserve or production total was confirmed. WUG data is dated 2003. Extent is derived from 5,800 km2 assuming 2:1.
entries.map_status: row coal-upper-silesia, 0 km from its centre

entries.name: Donbas, Donets Basin
entries.coord_basis: Donetsk city from Wikipedia, equal to the existing map row. A city in the basin, not a basin centroid; no basin coordinate found.
entries.figure: About 60 Bt; other estimates run from over 10 Bt proven to over 90 Bt remaining. 25.3 Mt in 1913, 83.7 Mt in 1940
entries.grade_or_note: Area 53,201 km2 (infobox), about 23,000 km2 for Donbas proper, about 50,000 km2 for Old and New Donbas. MAP CHECK coal-donbas (48.02, 37.80) r110: 38,013 km2, between the two area figures, acceptable. War has closed most mines: one report says 15 of 114 in Donetsk region remain functional.

entries.name: Ruhr
entries.coord_basis: Existing map row, about 3 km from Bochum (51.48, 7.22, Wikipedia). A city in the coalfield, not a coalfield centroid.
entries.figure: About 115 Mt per year in 1960, about 19 Mt per year in 2003; mining ended December 2018 at Prosper-Haniel
entries.grade_or_note: Hard coal, closed. About 4,500 km2, about 120 seams to 2,000 m, about 200 Bt by a 1984 estimate. MAP CHECK coal-ruhr (51.50, 7.25) r40: 5,027 km2 against 4,500 km2, a good fit.
entries.source_org: Visuotine lietuviu enciklopedija; press for closure
entries.unconfirmed_detail: A single encyclopedia entry supplies area and output; no BGR or RAG figures and no cumulative tonnage found. The 200 Bt is a 1984 estimate. Extent is derived from 4,500 km2 assuming 9:5.
entries.map_status: row coal-ruhr, 0 km from its centre

entries.name: South Wales Coalfield
entries.coord_basis: Rhondda from Wikipedia, equal to the existing map row. A valley in the coalfield, not a measured centroid.
entries.figure: 56.83 million tons in 1913 (51.997 million bituminous, 4.833 million anthracite)
entries.grade_or_note: Bituminous coal and anthracite, about 1,000 sq mi or 2,590 km2, 89 miles east to west and 21 miles wide. Last deep mine, Tower, stopped in January 2008. MAP CHECK coal-south-wales (51.62, -3.42) r40: 80 km across against a field 143 km long and 34 km wide, so an ellipse fits far better; area 5,027 km2 is about twice the true figure.
entries.source_org: Grace's Guide reprint of Aberconway, The Basic Industries of Great Britain
entries.unconfirmed_detail: A 1920s source, no British Geological Survey dimensions found. Long tons likely. Centroid not measured. No cumulative tonnage.
entries.map_status: row coal-south-wales, 1 km from its centre

entries.name: Nord-Pas-de-Calais Mining Basin
entries.coord_basis: Midpoint of Valenciennes (50.36, 3.52) and Bethune (50.53, 2.64) from Wikipedia. Sources place the basin running from Valenciennes to Bray through Douai, Lens and Bethune.
entries.figure: 2 to 2.4 Bt extracted in total; last coal 21 December 1990 at Oignies
entries.grade_or_note: Closed, UNESCO World Heritage 2012. Width never exceeds 12 km. MAP CHECK coal-nord-pas-de-calais (50.46, 3.55) r35: the row sits about 12 km north of Valenciennes at the east end, about 33 km east of the midpoint, and its circle stops near 3.06 E, so the Lens and Bethune half is outside. Move to about (50.44, 3.08) and use a thin east-west shape.

caveats: CONFIRMED RULE: yes means the figure, the coordinate and the extent were each seen directly, with the figure from an authoritative source. partial means at least one of those was derived, stale, from a lesser source, or only in a snippet with a problem. Every entry has at least one figure actually seen, so none is no, but many partial entries are weak: read unconfirmed_detail before using a number.

EXTENT: extent_km of 0 means no source gave that dimension and no defensible derivation existed, it does not mean zero. Where a value is derived from a stated area with an assumed aspect ratio, or from town spacing, unconfirmed_detail says so. Town spacing values are lower bounds.

COORDINATES: most are towns, mines or Wikipedia infobox points, not measured basin centroids. No GIS outline was used. Midpoints and distances are my own arithmetic, done by hand on a spherical approximation, not checked by a tool.

MAP CHECK SUMMARY of the 11 existing rows. Should change: coal-nord-pas-de-calais (sits at the east end, move to about 50.44, 3.08, thin 120 by 12 km), coal-kuzbass (about 127 km too far north, centre about 54.22, 86.34, 400 by 120 km). Depends on intent: coal-witbank-highveld (misses Secunda, 71 km south), coal-jharia-damodar (misses Raniganj, 72 km east), coal-ekibastuz (r30 is about 46 times the 62 km2 deposit), coal-south-wales (circle vs a 143 by 34 km field). Fine: coal-ruhr, coal-upper-silesia, coal-donbas, coal-ordos, coal-pocahontas. Note coal-ordos's coordinate itself was not confirmed by a fetched page.

EI ACCESS: the Energy Institute site and the BP PDF returned 403, and the KPMG copy of the 2026 review exceeded the fetch size limit. Production comes from the Our World in Data CSV built on EI 2026, read in 100,000-character chunks; latest values were summarised by the page reader, and 'unit not stated' in the CSV is taken as TWh per the grapher page. India's 17.97 EJ cross-checks against the 17.9 EJ quoted from EI 2026. Reserves labelled BP/EI end-2020 come from Planete Energies quoting BP Statistical Review 2022 (https://www.planete-energies.com/en/media/figures/global-coal-reserves). EJ values are my conversion at 0.0036 EJ per TWh.

RESERVES: the two series differ. OWID's reserve figures are EIA data, in a CSV with no stated unit, read as tonnes. The EIA series lists Kyrgyzstan at 28.5 Bt, rank 9, which is absent from the BP/EI top 12 and looks odd; I could not explain it. EI/BP has not updated country reserves past end-2020 as far as I could see. Top 12 by reserves uses the BP/EI series, so South Africa is 12th there and 14th under EIA. Countries are listed as the union of the top-12 lists, 16 rows.

PDFS: The page reader returned compressed binary for the EIA tables, Ministry of Coal, CMPDI/GSI inventory, Indian Bureau of Mines and Polish Geological Institute PDFs. Local copies of the PDFs were not opened. Numbers from those documents come from web search snippets of them. Reading those saved PDFs could upgrade several Indian, US and Polish figures; EIA 2024 Table 6 and the GSI coalfield table are the most valuable.

SOURCES NOT REACHED: BGR Energy Study (bgr.bund.de connection failed, BGR values are only secondary quotes), Britannica (403), UNESCO (403), IEA main Coal 2025 had no province data. No USGS product named World Coal Assessment turned up; USGS coverage here is the National Coal Resource Assessment and the 2015 Powder River assessment. The Geological Survey of Pakistan, Council for Geoscience, MEMR and Rosnedra primaries were also not reached.
RANKING: my judgement, by current output first, then reserves, with closed legacy rows last. Basin output and reserves are not like for like, and Indian company tonnages are not field tonnages.

CAP OF 32: Xinjiang is one entry and Colombia is merged to fit. Considered but left out, with what was seen. Singrauli: NCL 139.00 Mt 2024-25, the largest omission by output, no coordinate fetched. South Yakutia: Elga 28.6 Mt 2024 and about 2.2 Bt reserves, Elga at 56.20, 130.64, Neryungri at 56.68, 124.67. Surat: GA EDR 7,949 Mt, Inferred 10,393 Mt. Galilee: GA EDR 11,207 Mt, Inferred 21,227 Mt, large but mostly undeveloped. Gunnedah: EDR 1,815 Mt. Lusatia: about 34.6 Mt 2025, 60.7 Mt 2019. Belchatow: 44.26 Mt 2022 (GEM), 520.49 Mt reserves vs 1,930 Mt elsewhere. Maritsa East: 34.2 Mt 2022, mineable 2,096 Mt, resource 4,574 Mt, about 240 km2. Afsin-Elbistan: 3.4 to 4.9 Bt, MTA table 4,642 Mt. Zonguldak: 1,319 Mt geological, about 526 to 550 Mt proven, TTK 1.1 Mt 2022. Kosovo: 12 to 15 Bt, Sibovc 990 Mt, 7.2 Mt 2018. Karaganda: 3,600 km2, no basin output found. Pechora: Vorkutaugol 7.2 Mt 2023, no basin total. Moatize: about 11 to 11.6 Mt capacity and peak, ownership and status conflict between sources, no 2024 output. Durham and Sydney Nova Scotia: nothing usable found.

DATA CONFLICTS LEFT OPEN: China 2025 is 4.71 Bt (IEA) vs about 4.8 Bt (official). IEA mid-year 2025 is internally inconsistent on Australia (434 Mt for 2025, then 447 Mt in 2026 described as a fall). APBI-ICMA's Xinjiang 55.29 Mt looks like a scale error. PRB Wikipedia text on Black Thunder being the top mine conflicts with a secondary summary of EIA Table 9 for 2024 that lists North Antelope Rochelle first.
VINTAGE: this was gathered 2026-10-30. EIA's Annual Coal Report for 2025 data is due November 2026, so PRB, Illinois and Appalachian figures will soon be superseded.

caveats: THIS LIST IS A JUDGEMENT. No global reserve table exists for stone: the USGS MCS 2026 dimension stone sheet lists US production only, with other countries and the world as NA. The ranking blends output, trade weight, heritage standing and map spread, and another researcher could reasonably order it differently.

Entries are not comparable. Figures mix tonnes, m3, money, quarry counts and designations, and blocks, gross extraction and carbonate waste are different things. Carrara alone runs from 0.6 to 5 million t depending on basis. World extraction shows the same gap: gross 313 to 318 million t against about 153 to 155 million t raw and about 92 million t used.

Country table source: Carlo Montani, XXX Rapporto Marmo e Pietre nel Mondo 2019, as cited in ICE trade agency notes, 2018 data, total 153,000. China, Italy, Egypt, Spain, Portugal, USA, Greece and Saudi Arabia come from the April 2020 note; India, Turkey, Iran and Brazil from the June 2021 note; 2020 values from the 2023 note. Montani's own tables were never seen. ICE labels the unit as million t, but the values only make sense as thousand t. India at 17% and Turkey at 7.8% check out against 153,000.

Country table rank limit: places 1 to 6 are stated, with Italy sixth. Places 7 to 12 are only the countries I named in the query, so an unnamed country could sit between them. Egypt, Spain, Portugal, USA, Greece and Saudi Arabia are confirmed as figures, not as ranks 7 to 12.

PDF limit: The page reader returned unreadable binary for every PDF tried (USGS MCS, ICE notes, NERC Mercian paper), and the IUGS 55 stones book exceeded the size limit. USGS, ICE, IBM, IAEG and Mercian figures were therefore seen only as search snippets, not read in the document. Saved PDFs were not opened by other means.

Extent rule: 0 means no extent was seen. I did not guess from memory. Values for Rajsamand-Udaipur, Telangana, Verona-Botticino, Monte Coto and Drama-Thassos are town-to-town distances computed from sourced coordinates. Values for Afyon, Macael and Marmara are equal-area shapes computed from a sourced area. Most coordinates are towns, not quarry centroids.

Industry versus quarry: Yunfu, Shuitou, Cachoeiro, Verona, Novelda and Kishangarh are processing clusters that handle imported stone as well as local stone, so they mark industry rather than a rock body. Shaq El-Thoaban was excluded for this reason: it is a processing zone in the Tora Maadi area of Cairo with no quarrying evidence and no output share found.

Map row summary. Good centres: stone-makrana, stone-marmara-island, stone-aswan, stone-portland, stone-pentelicus. Radius looks too large: stone-portland (r10 against a 6 km island) and stone-marmara-island (r15 against 12.7 km equal-area). stone-aswan r15 is unproven. stone-indiana-limestone sits about 9.5 km south of the belt midpoint and misses Stinesville at r25. stone-carrara is on the town, with the quarries to its east. stone-pentelicus r10 could not be checked.

Conflicts rejected or flagged: Makrana 19.20 million t per year on Wikipedia exceeds all Rajasthan marble in IBM data; Mahallat's 30 million t reserves against 2 million t per year; Macael national share of 40% versus 80%; Elberton's Granite Capital title has no statistics behind it. Rogers City's world-largest title and Monte Coto's world-largest title are claims, not rankings.

Source quality is mixed. Many district figures come from trade press, sellers, tourism boards, press releases or Wikipedia, because national survey data by district was not found. Several are 15 to 20 years old (Afyon 2002, Porrino 2003, Denizli 2005, Sao Thome 2005). Treat them as order of magnitude.

Near misses left out by the 26 cap, with evidence seen. Elberton, Georgia: granite mass about 35 by 6 miles, about 45 quarries, over 200,000 monuments per year (Georgia Encyclopedia and others, https://www.georgiaencyclopedia.org/articles/business-economy/granite/). Barre, Vermont: Smith Quarry 50 acres and 570 ft deep, no output found, tours ended 2025 (https://dec.vermont.gov/node/1942). Stanstead, Quebec: 7,000 m3 or more per year (Polycor spec sheet, https://dev2.polycor.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/StansteadGrey-Granite-SpecSheet-EN-2021-05-11.pdf). Bohus granite: outcrop 85 by 35 km, 7,000 workers at the 1929 peak (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015EGUGA..1714883S). Gallura: Rosa Beta granite designated 2019 (https://iugs-geoheritage.org/geoheritage_stones/rosa-beta-granite/). Bath stone: GHSR July 2019. Kolmarden serpentine marble: GHSR January 2019. Kota stone: over 80 mines and about 1,000 units at Ramganj Mandi (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramganj_Mandi).

Considered and not included for lack of evidence. Caen, Oppdal and Alta: the combined searches returned nothing on them. Bangalore: no volume found. Hubei: only a trade-site share of about 18% of Chinese marble split with Shandong and Guangdong; Macheng not found. Isfahan and Yazd: no district data; Mahallat stands in. Vietnam (Luc Yen in Yen Bai, Quy Hop in Nghe An): no current tonnage. Saudi Arabia: national 1,300 thousand t but no district data. Shandong Laizhou surfaced as a possible large Chinese district with no figure. Wiesbaden excluded per the research plan.

caveats: Red Book edition: a newer edition than the planned one exists. Uranium 2026 (31st edition, published September 2026, data as of 1 January 2025) is used throughout. Its PDF exceeded the fetch size limit and could not be read directly, so every Red Book figure here is as reproduced by WNA. The Uranium 2024 and 2022 country tables were not obtained (the NEA 2022 page returned 403 and its PDF host did not resolve).

UDEPO: no deposit-level data could be reached. infcis.iaea.org returned only its About page, which says the map is a snapshot from early 2017 and that the database was renamed UThDEPO in 2026. IAEA conference and TECDOC PDFs returned 402 or 403. Only search snippets were seen: 62,674,137 tU across 2,755 deposits in 2017, and 14,034,700 tU conventional including Olympic Dam. No ranking in this file comes from UDEPO.
Ranking is my judgement across resources, current output and history. It is not a single metric from any source.

extent_km convention: a source-stated dimension where one was seen (noted in the entry), otherwise the spread of located sites or a stated area drawn as a square. A value of 0 means no source supported a number, not that the feature is a point. Extents were never taken from memory.

Cross-page conflicts in WNA are unresolved. Niger 351,100 tU (Supply) against 289,606 tU (Niger page). Brazil 167,800 tU against 231,000 tU. Ukraine 161,300 tU against 184,474 tU. Uzbekistan 2024 output 4,000 tU against 5,200 tU. US 2025 output 534 tU against 831 tU. The country table uses the Supply and Production pages throughout. The differences may reflect in situ against recoverable tonnes, but no source says so.

Other cross-source differences. Australia: Red Book 1,701,600 tU to USD 130/kgU; Geoscience Australia 1,959 ktU total identified, 1,280 ktU EDR, 2024 output 4,656 tU against WNA 4,598 tU; the WNA Australia page says about 1.2 million tU. Canada: NRCan more than 588,000 tU below USD 50/lb, 14,327 t in 2024, against WNA 551,700 tU and 14,309 tU. World 2024 output: WNA 60,213 tU, Red Book 61,924 tU. China 2024: WNA 1,600 tU estimated, Red Book 1,956 tU.
Units: many deposit figures are in tonnes U3O8, not tU. They were left in the source's unit, and 1 t U3O8 is about 0.848 tU. Country table rows are in tU.

Most coordinates come from Wikipedia, as the research plan allowed, and are not surveyed. Rejected: Wikipedia's Husab Mine coordinate (-22.767,14.517), which contradicts that page's own text; Cameco's Inkai page pin (48.02,66.92), which is a Kazakhstan map centre; and Wikipedia's Witwatersrand Basin coordinate (-26.20,28.04), which is the Johannesburg ridge and not the basin.

Considered and left out to stay within 26 entries, cut on combined size and current output, with Khiagda and Beverley-Four Mile kept ahead of them as active producers. Kintyre, Australia: -22.338,122.072, 25,274 t U3O8 indicated at 0.62% (December 2015, WNA), 60 to 70 km south of Telfer depending on source. Caetite and Lagoa Real, Brazil: town -14.069,-42.475, about 10,000 tU at 0.3%, undated, the only operating Brazilian mine (WNA). Limousin and La Crouzille, France: Bessines town 46.110,1.369, 23,500 tU from 1948 to 1995 (French regional government document, search snippet only); no WNA figure found and no full Limousin total confirmed. Salamanca and Retortillo, Spain: Retortillo town 40.802,-6.360, 23,000 tU measured and indicated plus 29.6 million lb U3O8 inferred (WNA), plant authorisation refused. Mecsek, Hungary: Kovagoszolos 46.081,18.124, about 21,000 tU from 1958 to 1997 (WNA). If any of these are wanted on the map, the data above is enough to add them.

Tumas, Dasa, Imouraren, Budenovskoye, Inkai, Tortkuduk and Katco are covered inside their district entries, not as separate entries, because each sits within a district already listed. Other large resources noted but not entered: Kvanefjeld, Greenland, 228,000 tU (May 2015, rare earth co-product); Straz pod Ralskem, Czechia, sandstone around 160,000 t under a major aquifer; Bakouma, Central African Republic, 36,500 tU inferred; Letlhakane, Botswana, 43,730 tU; Dornod, Mongolia, 24,780 tU; Tiris, Mauritania, 15,300 tU measured and indicated plus 19,800 tU inferred.

Seen only in search result snippets, not on a fetched page: the IMWA 216,350 t and German Economics Ministry and IAEA 231,000 t Wismut totals, the La Crouzille 23,500 tU figure, and the UDEPO totals. Search results arrive as machine-written summaries, and fetched pages were also read through an automated extraction step, so numbers should be spot-checked before anything depends on one exact value.

It agrees with OPEC's world figure as quoted there, 1,572.459 billion barrels, and with EIA's quote of the UAE at 120 billion, but it was not checked line by line against OPEC. OPEC reports world crude output of 74.85 million b/d in 2025.

PDFS: The page reader returned EIA and USGS PDFs as undecoded binary. Data came from EIA's HTML versions under countries_long, USGS HTML pages, and search snippets of PDFs, and entries relying on snippets say so. Several EIA HTML pages are old: Oman January 2019, Kazakhstan June 2019, Azerbaijan September 2021, Colombia March 2022. One Read of a saved PDF was attempted and failed; no PDF extraction tooling was used.

CONFIRMED VALUES: yes means the headline figure came from an authoritative body or a national regulator's data and the coordinate and extent were seen. partial means the figure is secondary or GEM-compiled, seen only as an old snippet, or the coordinate is a proxy or disputed, or the extent is missing. no means no usable authoritative figure was seen for that entry.

EXTENT: extent_km 0 means not seen, never zero size; no value was filled from memory. Where only an area was seen, length and width are its equal-area square, marked as my derivation in grade_or_note. Million bbl/y were converted to b/d by dividing by 365. Distances are my equirectangular estimates, good to a few km.

GEM: Global Energy Monitor is a compiler, not an authority, and is used mainly for coordinates. Its figures trace to mixed sources and contain visible errors (Daqing 2024, cumulative units on Ghawar, repeated 204.4 for Marun and Gachsaran), so treat GEM-only figures as indicative. Coordinates marked exact by GEM may come from a ResearchGate figure.
